neighbours.label: the word just before a verb of making a creative work (write, tell, make, record), in talk about writing or filmmaking
fire: It took the author a decade to figure out how to tell her grandmother's story.
The director wanted to know whether he could make a film about his own childhood.
Writers often ask me how they can find the right voice for a memoir.
When did you realize there was enough material to write a second novel?
The screenwriter struggled with how best to adapt the book for the screen.
Students need time to develop an argument before they draft the essay.
I knew I would write about the war once my father opened up.
The band spent a year deciding how to record the new album.
quiet: It took the plumber a decade to figure out how to fix the old pipes.
The farmer wanted to know whether he could sell his land next spring.
Patients often ask me how they can sleep better at night.
When did you realize there was enough money to buy a second car?
The engineer struggled with how best to repair the bridge before winter.
Students need time to eat lunch before they go to class.
I knew I would move to Denver once my father retired.
The team spent a year deciding how to paint the new office.

notes: Peaks on to/can/would/how/there before verbs; output promotes write/writing/crafting/prose. Probe weak (how to write .18), so low confidence.
